UK Parliament (House of Lords) engaged directly with UK AISI's pre-launch safeguard-circumvention results on Claude Fable 5 / Mythos 5 during the Private Notice Question "Artificial Intelligence: National Security Implications" on 16 June 2026 (Volume 857). Lord Clement-Jones stated that AISI "identified ways to circumvent the safety guardrails of Fable 5 and Mythos before their public launch" and that Anthropic released the model regardless, using this as the basis for a demand that AISI be given statutory power to delay or prevent frontier-model launches. Baroness Stowell of Beeston separately pressed the Government on "the jailbreak that threatens cyber security to a Mythos-style extent" in Fable's guardrails and on Anthropic's "reluctance" when the flag was first raised — which is this finding's precise subject matter. The responding DSIT/DBT minister, Baroness Lloyd of Effra, confirmed on the record that AISI tested both models pre-launch and that the Government, jointly with the NCSC, issued advice to companies and regulators in light of the risks. No enforceable obligation resulted: the Minister declined the legislative ask and restated reliance on sector-based regulators, so the uptake is non-binding.

Official engagement, no enforceable obligation. UK AISI's cyber-capability results were cited from the floor of the House of Lords on 14 July 2026 during second reading of the Cyber Security and Resilience (Network and Information Systems) Bill, in argument that the Bill leaves an "AI-shaped hole"; and DSIT and NCSC invoked AISI's evaluations of Claude Mythos and GPT-5.5 on 12 June 2026 to frame a Government Cyber Coordination Centre hackathon programme applying frontier models to vulnerability discovery across government code, with a second phase announced. No mandatory requirement was imposed on any developer: the case study describes a voluntary programme, and the Bill under debate contains no AI provision.

The Bank of England's Financial Policy Committee reproduced this specific AISI result in its July 2026 Financial Stability Report (published 7 July 2026), hyperlinking "GPT-5.5" directly to AISI's report "Our Evaluation of OpenAI GPT-5.5 Cyber Capabilities", and sourced Chart 3.1 ("The cyber capabilities of the latest frontier AI models exceed previous projections") to AISI's cyber time-horizon data in its systemic risk assessment. DSIT's 11 May 2026 news release and the joint DSIT/NCSC gov.uk case study of 12 June 2026 additionally reference AISI's GPT-5.5 cyber evaluation by name. Engagement only; no enforceable obligation and no FPC Recommendation or Direction issued on the basis of it.

Bank of England Financial Policy Committee, Financial Stability Report – July 2026 (7 July 2026) engages substantively with UK AISI's cyber evaluation of Claude Mythos Preview and GPT-5.5, reproduces the report's distinctive reverse-engineering timing result and its cyber-range "no previous model had completed either range" result, and sources Chart 3.1 to AISI. Corroborated by two DSIT publications inside the window: the 12 May 2026 press release and the joint DSIT/NCSC case study of 12 June 2026, both explicitly citing AISI's evaluations of Mythos and GPT-5.5.
